messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm doing a focused pass on the release notes and changelog pages to fix broken anchors and migrate SDK snippets after the docs tree refactor. Found a handful of bad anchor links and outdated Python/TS examples.
kevin: thanks for the flag. do you have a list of the broken anchors you saw? I can take the SDK snippets if you want.
joel: I ran the anchor-checker script locally and it reports 18 failures in /docs/reference and 5 in /docs/guides. output: `anchor-checker --root docs --report anchors.json`
maria: pasted the top-level failures below (copied from anchor-checker):
- /docs/reference/auth#token-rotation -> actual anchor is `#token-management`
- /docs/guides/ops#batching -> removed during restructure (now under /docs/performance/batching.md)
- /docs/sdk/js#streaming-examples -> new anchor `#streaming-results`
kevin: cool — I'll handle the JS snippets and updating the TS examples to the new function signatures. please point me to the staging URL and the PR template to include a changelog note.
maria: staging is at https://docs-staging.redwood.ai (internal only). PR template is in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. For changelog entries, use the relnotes section under `/content/relnotes/` and follow the short-form bullet format.
samir: I can take the anchor redirects. Suggest adding permanent redirects in the frontmatter like: `redirect_from: ["/docs/guides/ops#batching"]` or add a small anchor page with a meta refresh. Which approach do we prefer?
joel: prefer redirect frontmatter where possible. fewer html files to manage. For the batching example, though, we should add a short note in the new page linking back to the old guide for context.
maria: agreed. I'll open a tiny helper PR to add redirect frontmatter for the high-volume anchors. Kevin — if you can submit a PR for SDK snippet fixes, tag it with `relnotes:fix` and mention which relnote it affects.
kevin: will do. planning to update three JS snippets and one TS example. quick question — do we want to standardize on usage of `fetch` vs `redwood.request()` in examples? some files use both.
mar ia: (typo) maria: My vote is to prefer the SDK convenience calls (redwood.*) in code samples, but include raw `fetch` in a short appendix for transparency. Add a one-line callout: "SDK helpers shown; raw HTTP example in appendix".
docs-bot: anchor-checker run finished. created report at `s3://internal-docs-reports/anchors/1788004321-report.json` and raised PR suggestion #6421 (automated) for obvious redirects.
samir: nice — I'll review #6421 and add comments where we prefer manual wording changes.
joel: action items summary: 1) maria: add redirect frontmatter PR for top 10 anchors; 2) kevin: update JS/TS SDK snippets & tag `relnotes:fix`; 3) samir: review auto PRs & add manual copy edits; 4) joel: run anchor-checker again after changes.
maria: timeline idea — redirect PR today, snippets PR by EOD tomorrow, review + QA Wednesday, final relnotes ready Thursday. Does that work?
kevin: timeline works for me. I'll push a draft branch tonight with the updates and include code blocks like:
```js
// streaming example (use SDK helper)
const stream = await redwood.stream({ model: 'kestrel-1', input: prompt });
for await (const chunk of stream) { processChunk(chunk); }
```
maria: perfect. when you open the PR, add a short snippet-to-relnotes mapping in the PR description, eg: `js-streaming-example -> relnotes/2026-03-xx.md` so we can reference it.
docs-bot: reminder: please run `npm run docs:build -- --local` before pushing to ensure linkcheck passes. Current CI linkcheck is flaky around image CDN 502s.
samir: also FYI — I'll run a small eval on the updated examples to ensure outputs still align with our sample prompts. If we detect a divergence, we'll mark it as a known issue in the relnotes.
maria: thanks all. I'll start the redirect PR and post the PR link here. ping me if you need me to pair-review any snippet diffs. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — pinged you on the draft branch.
(THREAD END)
